meta.method: Web search result snippets only. WebFetch/curl were unavailable, so no PDF drawings or datasheets were opened directly. meta.confidence_convention: Any field named in a product's 'unconfirmed' array was found in fewer than two independent sources, or the sources conflict. Where sources conflict, the manufacturer figure is used and the conflict is noted.

floorstander_back_panel.coordinate_system: Back panel viewed from behind; x = 0 at the panel centre line, y = 0 at the floor (bottom edge of the back panel). All mm.

port.note: If a flared port with a ~140 mm flange is used, it occupies about y 335-475 and x -70..70.

floorstander_back_panel.free_band_below_port_y: 18 to 355 (bore) or about 335 (flared port): 317-337 mm for a cutout

results.plate: Hypex FA123 / FA253 (360 long; cutout 336 long)
results.vertical_centered: BLOCKED. The plate needs y ~10-370 (plate 360 + floor). The free height under the port is only ~335-355, so it misses by ~15 mm (flush port) to ~35 mm (flared port). Raising the port to centre ~425 with a flush port would leave ~5 mm to the plate and ~35 mm to the label, which is too tight.
results.vertical_offset_beside_port: FA123 only, and only with a flush (flangeless) port: plate x 55-175, cutout x 67-163 (14 mm to the side wall). The FA253 cutout (111 wide) would overrun the 177 mm inner wall line by ~1 mm.
results.horizontal_rotated_90deg: FITS. Flange 360 on a 390 back leaves 15 mm per side. Cutout 336 inside 354 leaves 9 mm per side to the side-wall faces.
results.amp_compartment: Use the cabinet side walls as the compartment's ends. Lower shelf top at y ~101.5, upper shelf underside at y ~248.5, front wall ~90 mm in from the back panel's inner face. Inside: ~354 x 147 x 90 mm = ~4.7 L of air. Gross displacement ~6.2 L with 12 mm panels or ~7.0 L with 18 mm panels (7-8% of 88 L).
results.box_tuning_effect: If 88 L net drops to ~81.5 L with the port unchanged, Fb rises ~4% (32 -> ~33 Hz). The simple vent formula (k = 0.732) says ~2 cm more port length (about 18.8 -> 20.9 cm) restores 32 Hz. Alternatively, enlarge the gross volume by ~6.5 L. Recheck in your box model.

woofer magnet clearance to the compartment front wall

bookshelf_generic.FA122_vertical: Needs a rectangular back at least ~340 mm tall outside (cutout 291 + walls + margin) and at least ~150 mm wide. Horizontal is impossible on a 200-250 mm wide carton (315 mm plate). A plate of this size leaves no room on the back for a Nutrition Facts label of any useful size. The compartment displaces ~3.5-4 L gross (15-25% of a typical 6.5 in 2-way box).
bookshelf_generic.PWR-ICE125_vertical: 216 x 153 plate, cutout 202 x 139: fits a 200-250 mm wide back with 18 mm walls (inner 164-214), height at least ~240 mm. Deeper (75 mm). ~3.5-4 L compartment.
bookshelf_generic.KABD-250_board: 91.4 x 68.6 x 22.9 mm board on a small DIY plate (e.g. 120 x 100 mm aluminium). Negligible volume, and it can be sealed (low dissipation).

fit_checks.desk_generic: A 100 mm wide carton has ~64-82 mm inner width depending on wall thickness, and every FusionAmp is at least 120 mm wide. Use a KABD-430 or JAB4 board (~91 x 69 mm footprint for the KABD, inferred) in the base of the master carton or in a small external hub. Power it from an external 24 V SELV brick, so there is no mains in the speaker.

primary.mounting: Rotated 90 degrees (horizontal), centred at y = 175 where the terminal cup is now. Sealed compartment behind it, spanning the full inner width.
rationale: Three NCore channels map directly to woofer / mid / tweeter: 250/250/100 W @ 4 ohm, 150/150/100 W @ 8 ohm (Hypex).

Woofer headroom: 10*log10(150) = +21.8 dB over 1 W into 8 ohm. With a ~90 dB/W/m 12 in that is ~112 dB peak at 1 m before any DSP bass boost, about 3 dB more than the FA123. Substitute the real driver sensitivity.

The mid and tweeter channels have far more power than the drivers need. Set HFD's soft-clip / limiter to each driver's rating. HFD's default soft-clip assumes 4 ohm, so enter 8 ohm drivers' impedance and max power.
The DSP handles the planned 350 Hz / 2.2 kHz crossover, driver EQ, delay alignment for the waveguide tweeter, and 3 presets. FIR is available on current firmware.
XLR/AES/S-PDIF inputs with loop-through let one source feed both speakers. Each amp is set to L or R in HFD.
The plate fits only horizontally: 15 mm per side on the outside, 9 mm per side to the inner walls. It clears the port by 112 mm and the label by 267 mm.
Not airtight, so it needs its own sealed compartment of ~6-7 L gross.

budget.mounting: Identical CAD to the FA253: same 360 mm plate length and 336 mm cutout length, only 15 mm less tall (120 / cutout 96).
rationale: Same DSP, inputs and software as the FA253, about EUR 150 less per speaker.

The woofer channel is 75 W @ 8 ohm (125 W @ 4 ohm), so ~3 dB less bass headroom. That is fine for domestic levels with a ~90 dB woofer, but tight if the DSP adds a big low-shelf or Linkwitz-transform boost.
Design the CAD back panel for the FA253 and drop in either plate. An FA123 in an FA253 cutout needs a 15 mm adapter strip, so cut for whichever you buy.

lowest_cost_diy_option.model: Dayton Audio KABD-4100 + external 36 V SELV power brick + DIY 3 mm aluminium plate
lowest_cost_diy_option.notes: Fine for proving the active crossover concept, but power per load is not published (estimated ~60-80 W into 8 ohm at 36 V). It uses SigmaStudio, which is harder to learn than HFD. Keeping the brick external keeps mains out of the cabinet. A Wondom JAB5 (EUR 69.90, 6 ohm minimum load) is the EU equivalent.

primary.mounting: Vertical. Needs a rectangular back at least ~340 mm tall, which sets a minimum body height for the bookshelf carton.
rationale: 2 x 125 W @ 4 ohm / 2 x 75 W @ 8 ohm. A ~87 dB/W/m 6.5 in reaches ~106 dB peak at 1 m, plenty for a bookshelf.
Same DSP, software and workflow as the floorstander FA253, so one learning curve covers the whole range.
The 120 mm plate width suits a 200-250 mm carton. The ~3.5-4 L sealed compartment must be added to the gross box volume.
The label cannot share the back panel: move it to a side panel or shrink it. Use a front port or a sealed box, which suits DSP EQ.

budget.model: Dayton Audio KABD-250 (one per speaker) on a small sealed DIY plate + 24 V SELV brick
rationale: 2 x 50 W @ 4 ohm / 2 x 30 W @ 8 ohm. ~102 dB peak with an 87 dB driver at 8 ohm, enough for near-field and small rooms.
The tiny board (91 x 69 x 23 mm) takes almost no box volume and makes it easy to build a sealed plate.
ADAU1701 with SigmaStudio. Bluetooth input is built in.
Alternative: one KABD-4100 driving both speakers (4 channels, more power) from the master speaker.

alternative_if_back_is_short.notes: 216 x 153 plate (cutout 202 x 139), 2 x 125 W @ 4 ohm, FIR + IIR, and the software runs on Mac too. Airtightness unknown, so give it a compartment anyway.

rationale: 4 x 30 W runs both desk speakers active (2-way each) from one board, so only one DSP program is needed.
No plate amp fits a 100 mm carton; every FusionAmp is at least 120 mm wide.
Put the board in the base of the master carton or in a small external hub. Run 4-conductor cable to the second carton. 24 V DC only, no mains.
Set limiters in SigmaStudio. A 2.5 in driver handles only a fraction of 30 W.
Same concept (4 x 30 W @ 8 ohm, TPA3118, ADAU1701, Bluetooth 5.0). EU-sourced. Supply range and dimensions are still unconfirmed.

desk.noise_note: ADAU1701 boards have about 98-100 dB dynamic range. Hiss is audible at desk distance with sensitive tweeters, so add a resistive L-pad on the tweeter if needed.
